ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Designing Dataset-Agnostic MVS Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose to design a novel MVS Transformer architecture that can generalize across diverse datasets, including those with varying image resolutions, view angles, and depth complexities. To achieve this, we will introduce a learnable spatial attention module that adapts to the specific characteristics of each dataset, while maintaining a fixed set of parameters across all datasets. Additionally, we will incorporate a dataset-agnostic normalization strategy to reduce the impact of dataset-specific image statistics on the network's performance.
CONTROLS: Compare to existing state-of-the-art MVS Transformers, which are typically trained and evaluated on a specific dataset, and to a transfer learning approach where the fixed-eff template is trained offline on NYUSideWalk and evaluate on CulturalPlace.
COST: 12 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed dataset-agnostic MVS Transformer to achieve comparable or better performance than existing state-of-the-art MVS Transformers on a variety of datasets, while reducing the need for extensive dataset-specific fine-tuning. However, it may also introduce some additional computational overhead due to the learnable spatial attention module.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Semi-Supervised MVS Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the application of semi-supervised learning to the MVS task, where only a small subset of the training data is annotated with depth information. To achieve this, we will utilize a self-supervised learning approach that leverages the consistency between the predicted depth maps and the reconstructed 3D points. We will also explore the use of adversarial training to improve the robustness of the model to incomplete or noisy depth annotations. Additionally, we will investigate the effectiveness of our proposed approach on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare to supervised learning approaches, which require large amounts of annotated data, and to unsupervised learning approaches, which may not be as effective in leveraging the available annotation.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed semi-supervised learning approach to achieve competitive results with supervised learning approaches while requiring much less annotation, and to outperform unsupervised learning approaches in terms of reconstruction quality. However, it may also introduce some additional computational overhead due to the use of adversarial training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Efficient Multi-View Stereo Inference
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate efficient inference methods for MVS Transformers, which are critical for real-world applications where fast reconstruction times are essential. We will explore several efficient inference techniques, including: (1) quantization-aware training, (2) knowledge distillation, and (3) model pruning. Additionally, we will investigate the use of efficient compute hardware, such as GPUs with tensor cores and specialized MVS accelerators. We will evaluate the performance of our proposed efficient inference methods on a variety of MVS tasks and compare them to existing state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: Compare to naive inference methods, which can be slow and memory-intensive, and to existing efficient inference methods for MVS Transformers, which may have limited applicability or performance.
COST: 8 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed efficient inference methods to achieve significant speedups (up to 10x) in reconstruction times while maintaining high accuracy, and to be more efficient than existing methods in terms of memory usage and computational resource allocation. However, it may also introduce some additional overhead due to the complexity of the inference pipeline.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of View Synthesis on MVS Accuracy
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the impact of view synthesis on the accuracy of MVS results. We will explore the use of view synthesis techniques, such as and depth image based three dimensional modelling (diBaM) in conjunction with our existing MVS Transformers to generate novel views of a scene. We will then use these generated views to evaluate the accuracy of our MVS results and compare them to traditional MVS methods that do not incorporate view synthesis.
CONTROLS: Compare to traditional MVS methods that do not incorporate view synthesis, and to existing MVS Transformers that do incorporate view synthesis, but may have limited applicability or performance.
COST: 5 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed approach to achieve improved MVS accuracy and completeness, especially in scenes with large occlusions or detailed textures, and to provide a new state-of-the-art for the task. However, it may also introduce some additional computational overhead due to the complexity of the view synthesis pipeline.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Comprehensive Comparison of State-of-the-Art MVS Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose to conduct a comprehensive comparison of the state-of-the-art MVS Transformers, including our existing proposals (1-8), on a variety of benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics. This will allow us to identify the strengths and weaknesses of each method, and to provide a clear understanding of their trade-offs in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and complexity. We will also use this comparison to recommend the most suitable MVS Transformer for different real-world applications.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of all 8 proposals on 4 benchmark datasets and 5 evaluation metrics, including reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and speed.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our comprehensive comparison to provide a rich understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of each MVS Transformer, and to identify the best-performing method for different real-world applications. However, it may also be time-consuming and computationally intensive, especially considering the need to run multiple experiments and comparisons.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Attention Mechanism on MVS Performance
PROPOSAL: Implement and compare the performance of Transformer-based MVS networks with various attention mechanisms (e.g., vanilla attention, linear attention, attention restricted to epipolar-aligned windows, and attention restricted to epipolar line pairs) on three real-world MVS benchmarks (e.g., DTU MVS, MVS-Dataset, and Custom Dataset). Evaluate the networks using metrics such as reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and runtime.
CONTROLS: Compare attention mechanisms against each other and against a baseline feature pyramid network (FPN) without any attention mechanisms. Ablate different attention mechanisms to understand their specific contributions.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that attention mechanisms can improve reconstruction accuracy and completeness, but at the cost of increased runtime. Performance may degrade for smaller views and more challenging scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Analyzing the Effect of View Disparity on Transformer-based MVS
PROPOSAL: Investigate how the view disparity (i.e., the number of input views) affects the performance of Transformer-based MVS networks. Design an experiment where the same network is trained and evaluated on MVS problems with varying view disparities (e.g., 2, 3, 4, 5 views). Evaluate the impact of view disparity on reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and runtime.
CONTROLS: Compare the results across different view disparities against a baseline network trained and evaluated only on 2-view problems. Analyze the attention weights and feature maps to understand how the network adapts to increasing view disparities.
COST: 5 GPU-hours (in addition to the existing base setup)
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that Transformer-based MVS networks can handle increasing view disparities by leveraging the attention mechanism, but at a growing computational cost.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Attention Mechanism on MVS Performance with Depth-wise Attention
PROPOSAL: Modify the Transformer-based MVS network from proposal 1 to incorporate depth-wise attention (DWA) and compare its performance against the vanilla attention mechanism and the baseline FPN. In DWA, attention is applied separately to each feature channel, allowing for more fine-grained and adaptive feature selection.
CONTROLS: Compare depth-wise attention against vanilla attention and the baseline FPN, ablating the attention mechanisms to understand their specific contributions. Evaluate the performance using metrics such as reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and runtime.
COST: 5 GPU-hours (in place of the original 10 GPU-hours proposal, as DWA requires comparable computational resources)
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that depth-wise attention can lead to improved reconstruction accuracy and completeness compared to vanilla attention, while maintaining or slightly increasing runtime.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Exploring Feature Aggregation Strategies in Transformer-based MVS
PROPOSAL: Investigate different feature aggregation strategies in Transformer-based MVS networks, such as concatenation, summation, and weighted summation, to determine their impact on performance. Design an experiment where each aggregation strategy is applied to the output of the Transformer encoder and compared against a baseline network using concatenation.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of each aggregation strategy against the baseline, ablating individual components to understand their specific contributions. Evaluate the performance using metrics such as reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and runtime.
COST: 8 GPU-hours (mostly incremental to the existing base setup)
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that weighted summation can lead to improved reconstruction accuracy and completeness compared to concatenation and summation, but may increase runtime due to additional computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Pre-training on Transformer-based MVS
PROPOSAL: Explore the effect of pre-training a Transformer-based MVS network on a larger and more diverse dataset (e.g., ImageNet) before fine-tuning it on MVS tasks. Compare the performance of pre-trained and non-pre-trained networks on various MVS benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of pre-trained and non-pre-trained networks against a baseline network, ablating the pre-training stage to understand its specific contributions. Evaluate the performance using metrics such as reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and runtime.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (due to the larger pre-training dataset)
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that pre-training can lead to improved reconstruction accuracy and completeness, but may increase runtime due to the additional pre-training stage. However, the impact of pre-training may be limited if the pre-training dataset is not domain-specific (i.e., not relevant to MVS tasks).

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Analyzing the Effect of View Disparity on Transformer-based MVS with Multi-View Attention
PROPOSAL: Modify the Transformer-based MVS network from proposal 2 to incorporate multi-view attention, which allows the network to selectively focus on relevant views when processing the input data. Investigate how multi-view attention affects the performance of the network on MVS problems with varying view disparities.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the network with multi-view attention against a baseline network without this feature, ablating the multi-view attention mechanism to understand its specific contributions. Evaluate the performance using metrics such as reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and runtime.
COST: 5 GPU-hours (with existing base setup, instead of additional 5 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that multi-view attention can lead to improved reconstruction accuracy and completeness, especially in scenarios with large view disparities, but may increase runtime due to the additional attention mechanism.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Grid Sampling on Transformer-based MVS
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of different grid sampling strategies (e.g., fixed-grid, adaptive-grid, and depth-dependent grid) on the performance of Transformer-based MVS networks. Design an experiment where each grid sampling strategy is applied to the input images and compared against a baseline network using fixed-grid sampling.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of each grid sampling strategy against the baseline, ablating individual components to understand their specific contributions. Evaluate the performance using metrics such as reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and runtime.
COST: 12 GPU-hours (mostly incremental to the existing base setup)
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that grid sampling has a significant impact on the performance of Transformer-based MVS networks, with adaptive-grid sampling leading to improved reconstruction accuracy and completeness, but may also increase runtime due to the increased computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Evaluating the Performance of Transformer-based MVS on Real-World Scenarios
PROPOSAL: Design a real-world dataset (e.g., MVS benchmarking scenarios obtained from public datasets) that is challenging in terms of camera noise, illumination, and other real-world factors. Implement a Transformer-based MVS network using the best-performing design from previous experiments and evaluate its performance on this real-world dataset.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the Transformer-based MVS network against state-of-the-art methods for real-world MVS, evaluating the robustness and generalizability of the proposed approach.
COST: 30 GPU-hours (due to the complexity and size of the real-world dataset)
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that the Transformer-based MVS network, fine-tuned using the best-performing design from previous experiments, can lead to improved reconstruction accuracy and completeness in real-world scenarios, despite potential challenges such as noise and illumination.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Training Objectives on Transformer-based MVS
PROPOSAL: Design an experiment to explore the effect of different training objectives (e.g., photometric consistency loss, geometric consistency loss, and a combination of both) on the performance of Transformer-based MVS networks. Compare the performance of each training objective against a baseline network trained with photometric consistency loss only.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of each training objective against the baseline, ablating individual components to understand their specific contributions. Evaluate the performance using metrics such as reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and runtime.
COST: 15 GPU-hours (mostly incremental to the existing base setup)
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that combining photometric consistency loss with geometric consistency loss can lead to improved reconstruction accuracy and completeness, but may increase runtime due to the additional computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Tensor Decomposition for Efficient Transformer-based MVS
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of tensor decomposition methods (e.g., Tucker decomposition and CP decomposition) on reducing the computational cost of Transformer-based MVS networks while maintaining performance. Compare the performance of the decomposed networks against a baseline network with no decomposition.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of each tensor decomposition method against the baseline, ablating individual components to understand their specific contributions. Evaluate the performance using metrics such as reconstruction accuracy, completeness, and runtime.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (due to the complexity and computational cost of tensor decomposition)
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that tensor decomposition can lead to significant reductions in computational cost while maintaining or slightly increasing reconstruction accuracy and completeness. However, the impact of tensor decomposition may be limited by the quality of the decomposition, and may not be suitable for all scenarios.

CONTROLS: Compare with a strong regular transformer baseline and the previously proposed models.
COST: estimated 500 gpu-hours

ACTION: ADD
title: investigate efficiency vs. accuracy trade-offs of epipolar window attention vs. linear attention
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of epipolar window attention and linear attention variants of Transformer-based MVS networks on the DTU and ETH3D benchmark datasets, assessing the trade-off between model accuracy and computational efficiency. We will implement both variants within the same network architecture, allowing for direct comparison of the two methods.
CONTROLS: Conduct identical experiments without both attentions' techniques to serve as our baseline; consider ablating each attention type to diagnose performance differences.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Epipolar window attention may provide a slight boost in accuracy compared to linear attention but at increased parameterization and computation; linear attention may be sufficient for real-world scenes if its negligible overhead aligns with real-world reconstruction priorities.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: studying pre-trained transformer architectures suitable for depth estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the suitability of different pre-trained Transformer architectures, such as ViT and DETR, as feature extractors for depth estimation in MVS, comparing their performance on DHM and Heman datasets. We'll integrate the Transformers into a coarse-to-fine depth estimation pipeline, focusing on preserving their global context modeling abilities.
CONTROLS: Conduct identical experiments with different pre-trained architectures, use random initialization for comparison.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Pre-trained architectures might be less effective as feature extractors for MVS depth estimation compared to lightweight architectures optimized for this specific task, yet exhibit strong performance due to contextual knowledge transfer from related tasks.

ACTION: ADD
title: design fast and accurate multi-scale feature aggregation
PROPOSAL: Develop a hybrid feature aggregation module that efficiently aggregates features from different scales and transformers within the MVS network; this will be evaluated on ETH3D and DTU datasets. The proposed aggregation strategy should balance accuracy and efficiency.
CONTROLS: Compare performance with direct concatenation and summations of features, assess effect of omitting different modules.
COST: 75 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach may offer improved feature combination quality compared to direct methods, at the expense of higher computational complexity unless selective optimization helps control this.

title: developing lightweight attention variants with domain expertise
PROPOSAL: Introduce specialized, domain-specific attention mechanisms to leverage the inherent structure of multi-view stereo geometry, such as using the viewpoint information as attention weights in a new transformer attention method. Evaluate the performance of these lightweight variants on DTU, ETH3D, and KITTI-3D datasets.
CONTROLS: Implement attention without viewpoint information as baseline; compare attention mechanisms that limit attention to epipolar lines/regions with proposed variant.
COST: 90 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Considerable performance enhancement is anticipated from the proposed direction using viewpoint attention compared to standard attention due to structural fitting in a given scene, aligning local spatial characteristics.

CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed approach with existing architectures, in particular with those that stop increasing spatial resolution stages early.
